neighbours.label: a reference to some other place beyond the one under discussion ('elsewhere in', 'other states', 'adjoining', 'an hour away in')
fire: Workers there earn far less than their colleagues elsewhere in Europe.
Their schools are doing worse than schools in other provinces.
The fire soon spread into the adjoining districts of the city.
A similar cottage just three hours away in Lyon costs far more.
Fishermen compared their catch with crews from neighbouring harbours.
Wolves have since moved into the adjacent valleys of the range.
Farmers in this valley sell cheaper than those in other regions.
Tickets cost half as much in nearby Salzburg, only two hours away.
quiet: Workers there earn far less than they did before the strike.
Their schools are doing worse than they did under the old head.
The fire soon spread along the wooden stairs of the theatre.
A similar cottage right here in the middle of Lyon costs far more.
Fishermen compared their catch with last year's on the long quay.
Wolves have since moved through the deep snow of the winter.
Farmers in this valley sell cheaper at the end of each season.
Tickets cost half as much on weekday mornings before ten o'clock.

notes: Probing: 0.18 to 0.67 against under 0.12 for same-place near misses, though 'elsewhere in Spain' read only 0.18. The - pole peaks on ' opposite' and ' different', so both sides may concern otherness; I did not test that link.
